Definition: from G1321; instruction (the act or the matter):--doctrine, hath been taught.
BiblicalUsage: Teaching is the doctrine itself, what is taught, and the Gospels measure every teacher by it. The crowds are astonished at Jesus' doctrine, the apostles continue steadfastly in it, and Paul warns that the time will come when men will not endure sound doctrine.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe doctrine is not the enemy of devotion but its backbone. The teaching of Christ astonished the crowds because it had authority, and the church stands or falls by whether it keeps that teaching pure.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
